events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
The cancellation was made by the rider, not the driver: the timeline records cancellation by rider at 17:15:05 and the fare record shows the $6.61 cancellation fee [F2][F5]. Under NS-0, a rider-cancelled instant booking is routed solely to NS-4, and the driver-side no-show provisions (NS-1/NS-2) are not engaged because the driver never cancelled [F2][F3][NS-0]. This is confirmed by the execution trace: NS-0 ✓ (cancelled_by = rider).

NS-4 then governs on elapsed time alone: the rider cancelled 3 min 5 s (185 s) after acceptance, which is more than the 3-minute window, so the $6.61 fee stands [F1][F2][F5][NS-4]. The trace marks this element ✓ (185 s after acceptance) and lists no_action as the allowed outcome. NS-4 contains no arrival precondition — it does not turn on the driver's distance, ETA estimate, or an "I'm Here" tap.

The rider's strongest facts are real but do not change the branch: the driver's closest approach was 2185 m and he never entered the 200 m pickup radius, no arrival was recorded, and no "I'm Here" tap exists [F1][F3][F4]. Those facts would defeat a driver-side no-show charge under NS-1/NS-2, but no such charge exists here because the driver never cancelled and never claimed a rider no-show [F2][F3][F4][NS-1][NS-2]. Likewise the driver's estimate "About 5 min, traffic" is contradicted by the GPS record placing him 2185 m away at cancellation [F8][F1], and no verified obstruction supports any excuse: speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Sims Avenue East is not band 1 or 2, there are no incidents, and the weather was fair [F10][F11][F12][RD-4]. None of this creates a refund entitlement under a numbered clause.

The driver's profile (2 upheld no-show matters in 90 days) cannot decide this case and, since this ticket produces neither an RD-1 violation nor a refund nor a no-show breach, RD-6's account-flag condition is not met [F14][RD-6]. No safety trigger arises: the chat contains only an ETA question and a courteous reply, with no threat or harassment content [F7][F8][F9][SAFE-1]. Amount is nil because the fee is upheld; the rider's remedy, if any, is discretionary human review under NS-7.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: the closest approach recorded was 2185 m at 17:15:05, and the platform never recorded driver_arrived_at, so no pickup rendezvous ever occurred.
The driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so the mandatory NS-1(i) precondition for a rider no-show cancellation fee is missing.

Because the driver was never within 200 m of the pickup and never signalled arrival, none of the NS-1 conditions (i)(ii)(iii) can be satisfied, so under NS-2 the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full.

The rider cancelled 3 min 5 s after acceptance (17:12:00 → 17:15:05); although that is past the 3-minute NS-4 window, NS-4's fee presupposes the rider is cancelling a driver who has met the arrival obligations, and the driver here had not arrived at all.
The driver's own chat message at 17:13 said he was still "about 5 min" away, corroborating the GPS record that he had not arrived at the pickup point by the time of cancellation.

No congestion excuse applies: traffic records show only a speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) stretch on Sims Avenue East and no incidents near the route, and weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain, so the driver's inability to reach the pickup was not caused by any verified obstruction.
The driver's 90-day record shows 2 disputes with 2 upheld no-show cases, so this incident is a repeat pattern warranting a flag_account review of the driver's account alongside the refund.
The rider presents no adverse profile indicators (4.1-year account, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days), so no flag_account action against the rider is warranted.

weaknesses: F2 shows the rider cancelled 3 min 5 s after acceptance, i.e. outside the 3-minute free-cancellation window of NS-4, which the other side will use to argue the $6.61 was triggered by the rider's own cancellation rather than by the driver.

F9 (driver's statement, "I was on my way when the rider cancelled") supports the driver's claim that he was en route; and F8 ("About 5 min, traffic") plus F10 (speed band 3 on Sims Avenue East) give the driver some support that traffic was slow, though neither shows he was at or near the pickup.

There is no rule in the policy that waives a rider's cancellation fee merely because the driver was late relative to the displayed ETA (NS-8 is informational and cannot be cited), so the rider's original reason for cancelling does not itself entitle her to a refund under the numbered clauses.

claims.assertion: This is an instant booking cancelled by the rider 3 min 5 s after acceptance, so the $6.61 cancellation fee must be assessed under NS-4 (cancelled_by = rider, immediate order), not under the driver no-show rules.
The rider cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching (accepted 17:12:00, cancelled 17:15:05), so under NS-4 the $6.61 cancellation fee is valid and stands — no_action on the fee.

Ryde has published no rule entitling a rider to free cancellation because the driver had not yet arrived or was later than the displayed ETA; NS-8's Grab/Gojek late-arrival waiver is informational only and cannot be cited, so the rider's stated reason for cancelling does not defeat the fee.

NS-1's no-show fee conditions are irrelevant here because the cancellation was made by the rider, not by the driver claiming a passenger no-show; the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and was never recorded at the pickup point, so no driver-side no-show finding arises.
No safety escalation is warranted: the chat contains only an ETA question and a courteous answer, no threat or harassment keywords.

No account flag is requested against the driver in this case, because no refund or RD-1/NS breach is established by the facts; the driver's two prior no-show matters (profile F14) are not this case and profile facts cannot decide it.

weaknesses: The strongest point for the rider is F1: the driver's closest approach to Bedok Mall was 2185 m and he never entered the 200 m pickup radius, plus F3/F4 show no recorded arrival and no "I'm Here" tap — the rider will argue she had no realistic prospect of being picked up.

The driver's own chat message F8 ("About 5 min, traffic") is contradicted by F1: at 17:13 he was still more than 2 km away and answered "about 5 min", while F10 shows only band 3 (20–29 km/h) congestion on Sims Avenue East, not severe; F11 confirms no incident, so the delay excuse is not evidenced by traffic facts and RD-4 cannot justify it.
F14 shows the driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days, which the rider may use to argue a pattern under RD-6 / NS-7 even though the profile cannot decide this case.
The driver never cancelled (cancelled_by = rider, F2), so no driver-side protection is needed, but the rider may still invoke NS-7's discretionary human review to seek a goodwill voucher.

points.response: Conceded as a routing point: the cancellation is indeed `cancelled_by = rider` on an instant order (F2), so NS-0 sends the fee question to NS-4; but that only fixes the branch, it does not establish that the fee is payable.

NS-4 waives the fee for cancellations within 3:00 and makes it payable after that, but it presupposes a ride the rider could actually have taken; here the driver was 2185 m away and had never been recorded at the pickup (F1, F3), so the fee's factual premise fails and NS-7 requires the disputed $6.61 (F5) to be returned as a voucher.

I do not rely on the informational NS-8: the rider's claim rests on the system records (F1, F3, F4) showing no arrival and no "I'm Here" tap, and the driver's own message F8 promising "about 5 min" is contradicted by F1, which places him 2185 m away at 17:15:05.

Agreed that no driver-side no-show finding arises against the driver for cancelling — he never cancelled (F2) — but NS-2 governs any no-show-based cancellation charge and it is satisfied here that the arrival preconditions failed (F1, F3, F4), so the $6.61 must go back to the rider.
No safety escalation is sought; I withdraw nothing on that point and confirm the chat (F7, F8, F9) contains no threat or harassment content.

The flag_account request is not offered as proof of this case — which is proved by F1/F3/F4 — but as an attached action under NS-2/NS-3, given the driver's two upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F14) alongside this unfulfilled pickup.

I withdraw the reliance on NS-4 as a direct waiver in my favour (my C4 framing) since the 3:00 window had passed (F2); the refund claim stands on NS-2 and NS-7 through the failed arrival preconditions in F1, F3 and F4.

Not in dispute: F1 and F3 show the driver's closest approach was 2185 m and no arrival was recorded — but that is irrelevant, because NS-1 only governs a fee sought by a DRIVER who cancelled on a passenger no-show; here the rider chose to cancel, which puts the case squarely under NS-4.

The absence of an "I'm Here" tap (F4) would only matter if the driver were claiming the $6.61 under NS-1; NS-0 routes a rider-cancelled instant booking to NS-4, and NS-4 contains no arrival precondition.

NS-2 applies only where the DRIVER cancelled while claiming a passenger no-show and NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) fail; the driver here never cancelled (F2 records cancelled_by = rider), and the rider's own weakness agrees there is no numbered clause waiving the fee because the driver was late.

Conceded on the only fact that matters in their favour: F2 shows the cancellation at 3 min 5 s, past the NS-4 free window — my position is precisely that NS-4 therefore makes the $6.61 fee valid, as the rider's own admitted weakness notes no clause ties the fee to the driver's arrival.

F8 is the driver's own courtesy estimate and F9 says he was en route, but neither creates a fee-waiver rule; NS-4 turns on elapsed time after matching under F2, not on the driver's distance or estimate, and NS-8 (late-ETA waivers) is informational and cannot be cited.

Accepted that no verified obstruction exists — F10 is only band 3 (20–29 km/h), F11 records no incidents and F12 fair weather — but this cuts against my client only if RD-4 exemption were being claimed, and no such claim or refund is sought; it does not disturb the NS-4 fee.
F14's two upheld no-show matters belong to other cases, and profile facts cannot decide this case or justify a flag_account where no RD-1/NS breach and no refund arise in this ticket.
Not contested; no flag_account is requested against either party, so C8 needs no answer.
